classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate two AAS congruences and one RHS congruence to establish concurrency and the equal perpendicular distances that define the incircle.

content.prompt:
Prove that: In any triangle $ABC$, the bisectors of the vertex angles are concurrent, and the resulting incentre is the centre of a circle that touches all sides of the triangle.

Let the angle bisectors of $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ meet at $I$, and draw $IA$.

Draw the perpendiculars $IP$, $IQ$ and $IR$ to the sides $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$, respectively.

spec.description: Angle-bisector intersectionI and three perpendicular feet; AI is a construction.
spec.mathematics: I is the side-length-weighted incentre of the explicit triangle; P/Q/R are exact perpendicular projections, giving the supplied right angles and two bisected angle families.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens and necessary labels only; no calculated answers.

sizing.exceptionReason: Proof construction, source relationships and full10pt labels determine size; final width and height require source-side rendered review.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use congruence to prove that $IR=IP$, and that $IP=IQ$.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle BRI$ and $\triangle BPI$, $\angle RBI=\angle PBI$ (angle bisector), $\angle BRI=\angle BPI=90^\circ$, and $BI$ is common. Thus the triangles are congruent (AAS), so $IR=IP$.

Similarly, $\triangle CPI\cong\triangle CQI$ (AAS: the angle at $C$ is bisected, both feet are right angles and $CI$ is common). Therefore $IP=IQ$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use congruence to prove that $IA$ bisects $\angle A$.

answer.worked: Right triangles $ARI$ and $AQI$ have the common hypotenuse $AI$ and equal legs $IR=IQ$ from part a. They are congruent (RHS), so $\angle RAI=\angle QAI$. Thus $IA$ is the third angle bisector and all three pass through $I$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Why does the circle with centre $I$ and radius $IR$ touch all three sides of the triangle?

answer.short: Its equal radii $IR,IP,IQ$ are perpendicular to the three sides.
answer.worked: $IR=IP=IQ$, so the circle with centre $I$ and radius $IR$ passes through $R,P,Q$. Each radius is perpendicular to the corresponding side. Therefore $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$ are tangents, and the circle touches all three sides.
